summary: Deep technical review between Redwood (AE+SE) and QuantaHealth engineering on isolation strategies and operational plans for a pilot. Key focus: how Dedicated capacity guarantees and runtime guardrails compare to Hosted multi-tenant in terms of noisy neighbor risk, KV prefix caching behavior, batching configs, and quantization tradeoffs. Action: run KV stress tests, confirm network dry-run, and deliver pricing + pilot terms.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Emily Park (QuantaHealth - Lead ML Eng), Marcus Reed (QuantaHealth - Platform), Anita Shah (QuantaHealth - Security)
Shared: benchmark spreadsheet (drive.link/qs-kv-bench), runbook draft (drive.link/rw-runbook), compliance packet (drive.link/sec-pkg)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, um, we wanted to cover isolation and performance plans for the pilot — really practical, not just whiteboard. quick round of intros?
[00:18] Emily (QuantaHealth): hi, Emily here, lead on the ML infra side, we'll be running clinical summarization models against our queries, interested in tail latency and data controls.
[00:30] Marcus (QuantaHealth): Marcus — platform, I'll own the network side and measurements.
[00:36] Anita (QuantaHealth): Anita — security/compliance, quick questions on KMS and audit trails.
[00:44] Daniel (Redwood SE): hi folks, Daniel from Redwood infra, I mostly care about runtime, KV cache, batching and quant impacts — I ran the preliminary profiling you saw in the sheet.
[00:56] Sofia: goal for today: align on whether Dedicated is required for initial SLA, what runtime guardrails we propose, and the test plan. we'll leave time for security Qs at the end.

[01:20] Daniel: starting with noisy-neighbor risk: Hosted is multi-tenant with per-tenant fairness and soft isolation. that means in bursts you can see tail increases if a co-tenant pushes sustained long-context workloads. Dedicated is a fenced GPU pool — you get capacity guarantees and lower variance.
[01:45] Emily: can you quantify that? like, what magnitude of tail-latency delta have you observed?
[01:52] Daniel: on average for models similar to yours (7-13B family), we've seen hosted tail p99 increase from baseline 220ms to as much as 640ms under synthetic noisy workloads; Dedicated p99 stays around 240-320ms. now these numbers depend on sequence length, KV hit rate, and batching.
[02:20] Marcus: are those numbers from our sheet? I saw different numbers there — maybe from older runs.
[02:28] Daniel: right, the shared sheet has a cold-run vs steady-state table; I re-ran with your sample prompts but used a higher concurrency to emulate daytime load — that's the run linked drive.link/qs-kv-bench.

[03:05] Emily: how does KV cache change the equation? we rely on prompt prefix caching for patient histories.
[03:12] Daniel: KV cache is the big lever. high prefix locality drives both latency and cost wins. with a 70% KV hit-rate, tokens served from cache bypass full attention recompute, so p50/p90 drop considerably. hotspot eviction and shard balancing are where noisy neighbors can still impact you — if a co-tenant fills KV with large prefixes, eviction churn increases.
[03:45] Anita: eviction churn — does that show up in logs/audits? can we alert on abnormal evictions?
[03:50] Daniel: yes, we emit cache metrics per-tenant: hit-rate, eviction-rate, avg KV size. for Dedicated we give you a private metrics pipeline and retention; for Hosted we give per-token breakouts but retention is shorter unless you add the observability add-on.

[04:30] Sofia: practical tradeoff: Dedicated gives less variance and private metrics; Hosted cheaper and faster to start. typical customers start Hosted for dev and then Dedicated for production SLAs. but we want to see what QuantaHealth constraints push — do you need strict p99 < 400ms?
[04:52] Emily: yes, clinical UI needs a soft SLA — p99 under 500ms for the main query path. occasional spikes are tolerated but need alerts.
[05:01] Daniel: that SLA is feasible on both modes with proper batching and KV tuning. key is to pick batching targets that match UI concurrency — too much batching increases token-level latency.

[06:00] Daniel: demo note — our runtime supports continuous batching with latency floors; you can set max batch wait (ms) and target batch size. for low-latency UI we recommend batch_inflight=2 and max_wait=15ms for your concurrency profile.
[06:25] Marcus: with those batch_inflight settings how does throughput scale? we're talking sustained 300 req/s during peak.
[06:34] Daniel: sustained 300 req/s with short contexts and high KV hit rates is within Dedicated pool of 8x A100-class GPUs (roughly). on Hosted you'd need to rely on routing to multiple nodes — rate limiting and burst capacity helps but you won't get isolated guarantees.

[07:10] Emily: quantization — we plan to use an 8-bit quantized variant to reduce cost. what's the accuracy tradeoff?
[07:18] Daniel: quantization is model and workload dependent. for many decoder-only models, 8-bit Q8 gives <1% logprob delta on generation for short completions, but longer context can amplify artifacts. we recommend an A/B with held-out clinical prompts. also note quantization can change memory layout and KV cache footprint — increase or decrease depending on kernel.
[07:55] Sophia: [sic - Sofia] sorry, typo, uh — Daniel, does quantization affect eviction rate?
[08:01] Daniel: yes, if quant reduces per-token KV size you get effectively larger cache capacity; if kernel requires packing, it could reduce usable entries. we instrument that in the bench.

[08:40] Anita: from compliance: KMS/HSM integration — Dedicated allows customer-managed KMS with a private control plane, correct?
[08:47] Sofia: correct, Private/Dedicated options support customer KMS and on-prem control plane. Hosted can integrate with our managed KMS but if you require customer key rotation and HSM-backed storage, we advise Dedicated or Private.
[09:05] Anita: audit logs and retention — we need 12 months for requests metadata. Hosted default is 90 days?
[09:11] Sofia: Hosted default retention 90 days; we have add-ons for extended retention but Dedicated gives configurable retention and log export endpoints to your SIEM.

[09:50] Marcus: network: we plan VPC peering and private IP routing. any gotchas we should dry-run?
[09:58] Daniel: yes, typical gotchas: MTU/path MTU blackhole with large KV blob transfers, ephemeral port exhaustion if you use many small connections, and routing DNS for private control plane endpoints. we'll schedule a dry-run.

[10:30] Emily: can you walk through a failure scenario where a noisy neighbor causes a service impact on Hosted and how auto-fallback works?
[10:37] Daniel: sure — scenario: co-tenant launches long-context video summarization spike, they fill batches and push up memory churn increasing p99. Our smart routing detects SLO breaches and can do automatic fallback to a lower-capacity variant (smaller model or quantized variant) or route to Dedicated-compatible pool if customer has reserved fallback or to a different region. Fallback adds complexity: you need to validate degrade mode quality.
[11:15] Emily: so fallback to a quantized model might change outputs — risky for clinical content.
[11:20] Daniel: exactly — that's why we offer per-route canaries and automatic A/B checks. we pair fallbacks with regression evals on a curated prompt set.

[12:00] Marcus: let's talk about KV shards — is eviction global or per-tenant?
[12:06] Daniel: eviction is per-shard; we maintain tenant-affine shards to minimize cross-tenant eviction interactions. but when memory pressure hits node-level limits, eviction cascades can still require cross-shard balancing. Dedicated reduces that because the pool is only your tenants.

[12:50] Sofia: one operational idea: set hard KV quota per workspace for Hosted so a tenant can't blow up the cache. we can set alerts at 80% usage and soft throttles.
[13:03] Marcus: would throttles mean increased compute latency or request rejection?
[13:08] Daniel: soft throttle would increase queuing latency slightly; hard throttle would reject new cache fills or evict more aggressively. we can tailor policy.

[13:45] Emily: about benchmarks — your sheet shows a 'KV primed' vs 'cold' column; can you explain the methodology?
[13:52] Daniel: primed means we replayed a trace to warm the KV for prefix tokens that match your prompt patterns; cold means fresh boot. we used your sample dataset of 1.2M prefixes and replayed a 24h trace. priming raises hit-rate and reduces avg compute by 40-60% depending on prompt shape.

[14:30] Emily: curious about tail lat for longer context (2k+ tokens) — does KV still help?
[14:36] Daniel: partially — KV helps only for repeated prefix patterns. For very long contexts that are unique per-request, KV offers little. those cases rely more on kernel-level attention optimizations and batching efficiency. quantization's effect can be larger for long sequences because memory bandwidth becomes the limiter.

[15:10] Anita: from security: can we get per-request provenance and redaction hooks? we need to mask PHI before logs leave our VPC.
[15:20] Sofia: yes, Dedicated + Private control plane enables pre-ingest hooks — you can run a redaction function before any request leaves your network; we also support on-device token filtering.

[16:00] Daniel: turnkey pilot proposal: 4-week run, start Hosted for integration and smoke tests, then flip to Dedicated for the final 2 weeks of the pilot for SLA verification. during pilot we run the KV stress test, two quant A/Bs, and one network dry-run.
[16:23] Emily: timeline wise, that's tight but doable. Any blockers we should know?
[16:30] Daniel: main blocker is network connectivity and KMS provisioning. also we'll need sample prompts and the traffic shape — Marcus, can you share that?
[16:41] Marcus: yes, I'll hand over traffic histograms and a 48hr tail log dump by EOD Monday.

[17:05] Sofia: pricing note — Dedicated minimum is a monthly commit; for pilots we offer a short-term pilot seat with reduced commit brim, I'll send scenarios.
[17:15] Emily: does pilot Dedicated reserve exclusive GPUs or shared but capacity fenced?
[17:19] Daniel: Exclusive-GPU pools are possible; typical Dedicated is capacity-fenced but you don't get hardware single-tenant unless you request private nodes. for your compliance needs, fenced pools plus KMS + private metrics usually suffice.

[18:00] Daniel: quick deep dive on batching knobs: target_batch_size, max_wait_ms, max_tokens_per_batch. For low-latency UI we keep max_wait_ms small; for high throughput offline jobs you raise wait and batch sizes to maximize GPU throughput. watch out for tail amplification when many short requests coalesce.
[18:30] Emily: can you recommend values for our 300 req/s with avg tokens=120?
[18:36] Daniel: start with max_wait_ms=12-20ms, target_batch_size=8-16, and monitor p50/p90/p99; if p99 climbs, reduce target_batch_size.

[19:10] Marcus: monitoring — will we get token-level cost breakouts during pilot?
[19:17] Sofia: yes, we'll enable token-level and model-level billing reports for the trial; Dedicated also provides route-level cost.

[20:00] Emily: tests: what would you run for regression checks on fallback models?
[20:07] Daniel: set up a golden prompt set with clinical edge-cases and metric thresholds (bleu/rouge is okay but prefer generation likelihood diffs + human spot checks). run canary on 1% traffic and compare distributions before switching.

[21:00] [Speaker 2 - transcription glitch]: um, slight echo, can you hear me?
[21:05] Emily: yeah hear you.

[21:45] Daniel: about quant artifacts — we'll record logits drift and output entropy changes. small drift is expected but large divergence flags failure. we can set auto-rollback triggers.

[22:30] Anita: legal: for Dedicated pilot, will you sign a DPA that references Dedicated hosting?
[22:36] Sofia: yes, we have a DPA template that includes hosting mode; legal will push minor edits, but Dedicated/Private clauses are standard. I'll attach the packet.

[23:20] Marcus: network dry-run details? what ports/protocols?
[23:24] Daniel: standard gRPC over TLS for control plane, and private VPC peering for data plane. we use ephemeral ports for worker heartbeats. We'll send an exact checklist before the dry-run.

[24:05] Emily: any immediate red flags for our use-case?
[24:10] Daniel: only that your traffic has long-tail spikes — we want to see the 48-hr trace and priming patterns. if many unique long contexts, KV won't buy you much and Dedicated helps only by reducing contention.

[25:00] Sofia: let's capture decisions: pilot flow (Hosted integrate -> Dedicated verify), KV stress test, quant A/B, dry-run network. agree?
[25:10] Emily/Marcus/Anita: agree.

[26:00] Daniel: I want to surface a nuanced bit — prefix caching helps cost but can amplify privacy concerns if not scrubbed. make sure your prefix dataset strips PHI or uses hashed identifiers.
[26:16] Anita: yes we'll provide a sanitized dataset for the bench.

[27:00] Emily: will the runtime support model pinning for rollbacks?
[27:05] Daniel: yes, we support version pinning and one-click rollback with canary routing. we also provide a model catalog interface to set traffic splits.

[28:00] Marcus: what about autoscaling — burst vs scheduled?
[28:06] Daniel: Dedicated supports scheduled autoscale and burst to a defined limit; Hosted has burst but subject to overall capacity. autoscale triggers can be based on concurrency, queue depth, or custom latency SLOs.

[29:10] Emily: curious about storage costs for KV — is that included in compute or billable separately?
[29:15] Sofia: KV memory is part of compute SKU; persistent caches or extended shard stores may be an add-on. we'll put exact numbers in the pricing scenarios.

[30:00] Daniel: small demo note — I toggled a simulated noisy neighbor in the bench and recorded p99 jump; I'll share the clip and raw logs.
[30:15] Sofia: thanks, that will be helpful for your internal stakeholders.

[31:30] Emily: any recommended SLAs aligned to Dedicated sizes?
[31:36] Daniel: for Dedicated pools of that size we guarantee 99.9% uptime and p99 targets inside 450ms for typical 7-13B runs with KV hit-rate >50%. specifics in SLA doc.

[32:20] Anita: about data residency — can Dedicated be pinned to a specific region?
[32:26] Sofia: yes, region pinning available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted gives region preference but not strict residency unless on special contract.

[33:00] Marcus: for the dry-run, we'll need a checklist of firewall rules.
[33:05] Daniel: we'll send a 1-pager with IP blocks, ports, MTU guidance and test scripts.

[34:00] Emily: what observability will we have on KV internals during pilot?
[34:06] Daniel: metrics: per-tenant hit-rate, avg-entry-size, evictions/sec, lookup latency; logs: eviction trace and allocation events; traces: per-request KV lookups and bugtrace. for Dedicated we can forward to your Datadog/Splunk.

[35:00] [noise] Sophia: [sic] small background noise sorry.

[35:30] Daniel: one more thought: compression — we sometimes apply lightweight per-entry compression which reduces memory footprint but adds CPU to lookup path; on GPU-heavy workloads that's often worth it. we'll include compression experiments in the bench.

[36:10] Emily: ok let's talk deliverables and owners.
[36:15] Sofia: owners: Daniel runs bench (KV stress + quant), Marcus provides traces, Anita provides compliance redaction rules, Sofia sends pricing + DPA. expected dates we listed earlier.

[37:05] Marcus: I'll aim to get traces by Monday, and a skeleton firewall rule set by Tuesday.

[38:00] Daniel: also we'll instrument a regression harness that hits golden prompts and computes divergence metrics — expect an initial report within 72 hours of bench completion.

[39:00] Emily: good. will you share the raw bench scripts? we prefer to reproduce internally.
[39:06] Daniel: yes, we version the scripts in a repo and can give read-only access.

[40:00] Anita: any compliance gotchas for VPC peering with HIPAA data?
[40:07] Sofia: HIPAA-backed deployments must use Dedicated or Private with covered BAA; Hosted can be included under BAA only with specific safeguards; we'll get legal on that.

[41:00] Daniel: last technical note — KV eviction policy tuning: LRU works but for our workloads we often recommend hybrid LRU+frequency, because some clinical prefixes are rare but critical. hybrid reduces accidental eviction of low-frequency critical keys.

[42:00] Emily: interesting. is that tunable per-tenant?
[42:05] Daniel: yes, for Dedicated you can pick eviction policy per-workspace.

[43:00] Marcus: what's the rollback plan if the Dedicated flip produces unexpected output differences?
[43:07] Daniel: we do canary traffic split, automated regression checks; if divergence exceeds thresholds we auto-roll back and open an incident.

[44:00] Emily: edge-case — if we pin to a quantized variant for cost reasons, can we route only a percentage of traffic to full-fp?
[44:08] Daniel: yes traffic splitting by route and weight is supported. you can do weighted percentages and set evaluation windows.

[45:00] Sofia: we're at about 45 minutes; want to reserve last 15 for security/legal specifics.

[45:30] Anita: quick detail — SSO/SAML requirements and RBAC for console access?
[45:36] Sofia: Redwood supports SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access extraction. for Dedicated you can map roles to your IdP.

[46:30] Daniel: also note service tokens vs user tokens — for programmatic calls use service tokens scoped to workspace. we log token usage per principal.

[47:20] Anita: encryption at rest — default is provider-managed KMS for Hosted, can we bring our own for Dedicated?
[47:27] Sofia: yes BYOK for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports managed KMS only.

[48:00] Marcus: incidently, what's the support SLA during pilot?
[48:05] Sofia: pilot includes business-hours support and a dedicated SE touch; upgrade to 24/7 on-call is available for production contracts.

[49:00] Emily: can we get synthetic traffic generators you use so our ops team can rehearse?
[49:06] Daniel: yes we provide load scripts and a replay harness.

[50:00] Marcus: how do you measure tokenization differences between quantized and fp models?
[50:06] Daniel: tokenization is model-driven and independent of quantization; measurement happens at logprob level and edit distance on outputs.

[51:00] Emily: any recommendation on warm-up schedules to get KV to steady-state before peak?
[51:07] Daniel: yes, run a priming traffic batch 30-60 minutes before expected peak; for high-churn data we recommend continuous background priming.

[52:00] Daniel: summary recap: pilot flow, bench owners, network dry-run. Daniel to post bench baseline and noisy neighbor artifact; Sofia to send pricing + DPA; QuantaHealth to provide traces and redaction rules.

[53:00] Emily: sounds good. we'll take the bench and try to reproduce.

[54:00] Sofia: I'll share meeting notes and create the pilot workspace in the console with provisional creds.

[55:00] Anita: legal will circle on the DPA edits, expect comments.

[56:00] Marcus: I'll prepare the firewall checklist and trace dumps.

[57:00] Daniel: expecting to start bench Thursday if traces arrive Monday.

[58:00] Emily: ok thanks everyone. last question — is there an SLA credit model if p99 breaches during Dedicated verification?
[58:10] Sofia: yes SLA credits in contract; we'll outline thresholds in the term sheet.

[59:00] [crosstalk] multiple: thanks, bye.

[60:00] Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts and calendar invites for the dry-run.
[62:00] Meeting ends
